newSolution: \(p = \frac{1}{4}\), \(q = \frac{3}{4}\). \(P(\text{at least one success}) = 1 - \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^n \ge \frac{9}{10} \Rightarrow \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^n \le \frac{1}{10}\). Taking \(\log_{10}\): \(n(\log_{10} 3 - \log_{10} 4) \le -1\). Dividing by the negative quantity flips the inequality: \(n(\log_{10} 4 - \log_{10} 3) \ge 1 \Rightarrow n \ge \frac{1}{\log_{10} 4 - \log_{10} 3}\). This is option D. NOTE: the source booklet's key column marks \(\frac{1}{\log_{10} 4 + \log_{10} 3}\), which contradicts the booklet's own printed solution; that solution and this derivation both give \(\frac{1}{\log_{10} 4 - \log_{10} 3}\), which is the answer recorded here.
